OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is converted to
            E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept when present,
            otherwise the country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0'
            is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. So
            '0412 345 678' is stored and returned as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when
            omitted it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag supplied on create. When true, the owner is allowed
            to be registered even though another owner already has the same last
            name and address (i.e. they share a household). When absent or false,
            such a duplicate is rejected with a 409 Conflict.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of the owner's first and last
                name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                A generated identifier formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>', where LAST3
                is the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN
                is a global 4-digit zero-padded sequence.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object
      properties:
        content:
          title: Content
          description: Pet owners in the requested page.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Owner'

The refactor is complete and verified. Here's what I did and why.

## What I found

The only test in the project is `AcceptanceTest.coreJoinersShareHouseholdId`, and it targets the **upcoming** feature — it reads a `householdId` field off the response that doesn't exist yet. It fails today (baseline) with an NPE at line 21 because `householdId` is absent. Since the task explicitly forbids implementing the feature, this test **must remain failing for that same reason** — turning it green would mean shipping the change. Everything else (compilation, the existing duplicate-household rejection behavior) is what I had to preserve.

## The restructuring

The seam the change needs is in the household logic. Today `requireUniqueHousehold` computes the last-name-plus-address match as a throwaway boolean (`anyMatch`). But the upcoming `assignHousehold` has to actually *retrieve* the matching household member(s) to copy/share a stable `householdId`. A direct implementation would either duplicate the collapse-and-compare logic or cram the finding-and-assigning into a void validation method — which is exactly the "more complexity than it can hold" the prompt describes.

So I extracted the matching into a reusable, documented finder, `findHouseholdMembers(OwnerFieldsDto)`, returning the matched owners in `findAllOwners()` order. This mirrors how the controller already factors each concern (`requireUniqueTelephone`, `normalizeEmail`, `collapseWhitespace`, …) into a focused private helper with full Javadoc.

- `requireUniqueHousehold` now just asks the finder whether any member exists — behavior identical (`anyMatch` → `filter().toList().isEmpty()` yields the same rejection decision).
- The future `assignHousehold` / `householdId` logic and `addOwner` change can build on `findHouseholdMembers` and drop the shared-id assignment next to the existing `owner.setCustomerCode(...)` derivation, keeping each method small.

I did not touch `Owner.java`: adding the `householdId` field and its accessors is the change itself, and plain persisted accessors need no preparation.

## Verification

- **Compiles cleanly** — the suite ran, so the refactored controller built.
- **Behavior unchanged** — the response body in the test run is byte-for-byte the same as baseline (including `"sharesHousehold":null`), and the duplicate-household rule still holds.
- **Test state identical to baseline** — the single pre-existing failure (`AcceptanceTest`, NPE at line 21, missing `householdId`) is unchanged; no new failures, nothing regressed.

To be explicit: I did **not** make the acceptance test pass, because that requires implementing the feature this task told me to leave for later.
